title: Sellers and landlords that also appear in campaign, lobbying or vendor records
question: Do the companies that sold buildings to the City, or rent buildings to it, also appear as campaign donors or donors’ employers, as clients of registered lobbyists, or as City vendors?
finding: 93 company names were screened (30 sellers and 65 landlords; individuals and public bodies left out). 10 match a campaign contributor or a contributor’s employer, $432,184 in all, most of it Pacific Gas and Electric Company ($354,584; its deal here: seller of 5000 Hunters Point Boulevard (2026, $575,000)); 8 match a lobbyist’s client (Pacific Gas and Electric Company, 964 reported contacts; McDonald’s Corporation, 39 reported contacts; 200 Paul, LLC, 21 reported contacts); 0 match a payor of a payment made at an official’s request; 1 filed a major-developer disclosure; 47 appear as City vendors, which for a landlord is the rent. Most sellers and landlords are single-purpose companies named after one address, and they match nothing: the people behind them are not in these records.
how: Seller and landlord names as the Board file titles give them, companies only. Each name is reduced to its core (punctuation and endings such as LLC removed) and matched exactly against: contributors and contributors’ employers in City campaign filings since 2012, payors of behested payments, clients in the lobbyist activity directory, vendors in City payment records since fiscal year 2017, and filers of the major-developer disclosure. A row is shown when a seller matches anything, or a landlord matches anything other than being paid as a vendor.
limits: Every match is a name match and is labelled as one; two companies can share a name, and a contributor’s “employer” is whatever the contributor wrote. Campaign contributions, hiring a lobbyist and being paid rent by the City are disclosed. A seller or landlord with no match is not thereby unconnected: a single-purpose company hides its owners from every record used here. No individual is matched or named. This screen says nothing about price; for that the roll’s limits apply: it records no sale price, only a sale date and assessed values, and the recorded deed and transfer-tax declaration would settle what was paid.
